```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  ## Keep figures in the section that discusses them. Captioned figures are LaTeX floats,
  ## so by default two full-width 4800 px maps drift to wherever they fit -- which put them
  ## pages away from the text about them. `H` (from the float package, loaded in the YAML
  ## header) pins them exactly where they appear in the source.
  fig.pos = "H",
  out.extra = ""
)

## knitr evaluates chunks in the directory of the input file, so anything that resolves the project
## by falling back to the working directory (`workflowtools::findProjectPath()` among them) reports
## `reports/` and every derived path silently misses. Walk up to the directory holding `_targets.R`.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = FALSE)
  while (!file.exists(file.path(p, "_targets.R")) && dirname(p) != p) {
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  if (!file.exists(file.path(p, "_targets.R"))) {
    stop("could not locate the project root")
  }
  p
}

proj <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = proj)

## Emit native LaTeX tables rather than markdown ones. Pandoc turns a markdown table into a
## `longtable`, which splits across pages -- so a table lands half on one page and half on the next.
## `format = "latex"` with `booktabs` produces a `table` float instead, and floats never split; the
## preamble then pins them in place and sets them a size down.
options(knitr.table.format = "latex")

library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(targets)

## Artefacts of the published (pre-correction) run, copied out of the way before the rerun
## overwrote them. See section "Reproducing this report".
PUBLISHED <- file.path(proj, "Data", "processed", "published-2026-01-27")
## Derived from wherever `_targets` actually resolves to (it is usually a symlink to bulk storage),
## so no site-specific absolute path is baked into the repo. Override with the environment variable.
PUB_META <- Sys.getenv(
  "BC_CONN_PUBLISHED_META",
  file.path(
    dirname(normalizePath(file.path(proj, "_targets"), mustWork = FALSE)),
    "_targets_meta_backup_pre-2026-08-25-fixes"
  )
)
## Figures live beside this document, wherever it is. Building the path out of `proj` instead
## hardcodes the assumption that this file sits in `reports/`, and when project-root resolution
## slipped that assumption produced a nested `reports/reports/figures`.
rmd_dir <- tryCatch(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), error = function(e) NULL)

if (is.null(rmd_dir) || !nzchar(rmd_dir) || is.na(rmd_dir)) {
  rmd_dir <- file.path(proj, "reports") ## sourcing the chunks outside knitr
}

FIGDIR <- normalizePath(file.path(rmd_dir, "figures"), mustWork = FALSE)
dir.create(FIGDIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

## One place that decides how every table in this report is drawn.
##
## `HOLD_position` keeps a table with the text discussing it instead of letting LaTeX float it
## elsewhere, and the smaller size keeps the wider ones on a single page. Written with `kableExtra`
## rather than raw LaTeX in the document preamble, so it can be adjusted by anyone comfortable with
## R without having to read TeX.
##
## Captions are plain text on purpose: with native LaTeX tables the caption is passed through
## verbatim, so a stray underscore or backtick becomes a TeX error reported several pages away from
## the caption that caused it.
styled <- function(x, ...) {
  knitr::kable(x, ...) |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = "HOLD_position", font_size = 9)
}

ha <- function(x) sum(terra::expanse(x, unit = "ha", transform = FALSE))
num <- function(x, d = 1) formatC(round(x, d), format = "f", big.mark = ",", digits = d)
dur <- function(s) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(s),
    "--",
    ifelse(
      s >= 3600,
      sprintf("%.2f h", s / 3600),
      ifelse(s >= 60, sprintf("%.1f m", s / 60), sprintf("%.1f s", s))
    )
  )
}
have <- function(...) all(file.exists(...))

## `tar_read()` happily returns a target that has NOT been rebuilt: the store keeps the published
## run's object and metadata until the target is remade. Reading one of those and calling it
## "corrected" would silently compare the published run against itself. A target counts as rebuilt
## only where its recorded time differs from the published snapshot.
secs_by_name <- function(store) {
  if (!dir.exists(store)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  m <- tar_meta(store = store, fields = c("name", "seconds"))
  stats::setNames(m$seconds, m$name)
}

PUB_SECONDS <- secs_by_name(PUB_META)
CUR_SECONDS <- secs_by_name(file.path(proj, "_targets"))

is_rebuilt <- function(target) {
  if (is.null(PUB_SECONDS) || !target %in% names(PUB_SECONDS)) {
    return(TRUE)
  }
  if (is.null(CUR_SECONDS) || !target %in% names(CUR_SECONDS)) {
    return(FALSE)
  }
  cur <- CUR_SECONDS[[target]]
  if (is.na(cur)) {
    return(FALSE)
  }
  !isTRUE(all.equal(cur, unname(PUB_SECONDS[[target]])))
}
```

# Summary

A defect found in the seral-patch construction (commit `145cffb`) turned out to be one of several,
and together they invalidate the connectivity results published in January 2026.
This report documents what was wrong, what the corrected numbers are, what the rerun cost, and how
urgently the Omniscape runs need to be repeated.

The headline is that the two layers Omniscape actually consumes -- the composite resistance and
source-weight rasters -- change materially, because roughly half of what the published run treated
as old interior forest was not forest at all, and a further large block of genuine old forest was
modelled at the wrong resistance.
The Omniscape runs therefore need to be repeated; they cannot be patched.

A second strand of work, in the runtime section below, retooled the two largest spatial overlays.
Tiling the final resultant took it from 5 h 52 m to 18 m, and tiling the interior-forest overlay
takes it from 3 h 08 m to 6 m; both reproduce their outputs exactly.
That matters here because the corrections below had to be applied, checked and re-applied several
times over, and a step measured in hours is one that cannot be retried casually.
It matters more for what comes next: the workflow is intended to cover the wider Cariboo, and
Cariboo-Chilcotin alone is roughly 2.4 times Quesnel's area, with these costs growing faster than
area rather than in step with it.
The retooling is a prerequisite for that extension rather than a refinement of it.

```{r headline}
data.frame(
  Item = c(
    "Seral layer, total area",
    "Old interior forest",
    "VRI x NDT-BEC layer, double-counted area",
    "Pipeline steps eliminated"
  ),
  Published = c("2,931,558 ha", "326,081.5 ha (13,783 polys)", "15,449.2 ha", "--"),
  Corrected = c("see Section 3", "166,915.6 ha (10,348 polys)", "0.0 ha", "35.1 h of compute"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  styled(caption = "Headline effects of the corrections.", booktabs = TRUE)
```

# Defects

Each of these produced plausible-looking wrong numbers rather than an error, which is why they
survived into a published run.

```{r defects}
data.frame(
  Defect = c(

    "Old/mature-old patches were never filtered to INTERIOR_CATEGORY MO/O",
    "Interior forest overwrote `Seral`; the union propagated the wrong attributes",
    "Seral layer built with `sf::st_join()` instead of an intersection",
    "Leading group joined with `terra::union()`",
    "Sliver elimination used the area rule, not arcpy's LENGTH rule",
    "Patch statistics measured overlay fragments",
    "Omniscape tile overlap divided by pixel size"
  ),
  Effect = c(
    "mature+old interior forest came out byte-identical to old-only",
    "50.8% of `old interior forest` was unclassified land",
    "160,417 ha of old cores modelled at resistance 250 instead of 1",
    "layer inflated to 7.78 M polygons / 39.5 Mha",
    "22,628 ha of land dropped, 15,449 ha double-counted",
    "not the semantics the arcpy scripts this ports rely on",
    "smallest reported Old patch was 4.6e-6 m2",
    "artifact-ridden mosaic in the tiled benchmark run"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  styled(caption = "Defects corrected in this rerun.", booktabs = TRUE)
```

# Data corrections

## The VRI x NDT-BEC overlay

The leading-group layer is left-joined onto the VRI x NDT-BEC intersection.
This was done with `terra::union()` followed by dropping the leading-group-only parts.
`terra::union()` is wrong here: it emits output polygons that overlap one another, and its dissolved
footprint is smaller than its input, so it double-counts some land and drops other land outright.
The two errors act in opposite directions, which is why the published total looked only slightly low
rather than obviously broken.

`terra::intersect()` plus `terra::erase()` partitions the input exactly.

```{r vri-becndt}
data.frame(
  Measure = c("features", "sum of parts (ha)", "dissolved footprint (ha)", "double-counted (ha)"),
  Published = c("400,534", "3,534,286.2", "3,518,837.1", "15,449.2"),
  Corrected = c("398,109", "3,541,465.4", "3,541,465.4", "0.0"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  styled(
    caption = paste(
      "VRI x NDT-BEC overlay, whole study area.",
      "In the corrected layer the parts sum exactly to the area they cover."
    ),
    booktabs = TRUE
  )
```

## The `terra::union()` defect

The single largest cause of wrong numbers here was one function, reached for in three separate
places because the project's own notes recommended it: `terra::union()` has exactly the overlay
semantics the arcpy scripts need, and produces silently wrong results on this data.

It fails in two directions at once, which is why the totals looked plausible rather than broken. Its
output polygons overlap one another, so their areas sum to more ground than they cover; and the
ground they cover is smaller than the inputs, so land goes missing. The two errors partly cancel.

```{r union-defect}
data.frame(
  Where = c(
    "VRI x NDT-BEC overlay (study area)",
    "Final resultant (2,933-polygon window)",
    "Minimal case (7 polygons)"
  ),
  `Counted twice` = c("15,449 ha", "303 ha", "5.7 ha"),
  `Land lost` = c("22,628 ha", "82 ha", "1,203 ha"),
  `Slower by` = c("418x", "28.5x", "--"),
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  styled(caption = "The same defect measured at three scales.", booktabs = TRUE)
```

Three things about it are worth recording, because each one delayed finding it.

It is not a version problem. The identical numbers come out under terra 1.8.86 and 1.9.34, on both
R 4.5.3 and R 4.6.1, with GDAL 3.8.4 and GEOS 3.12.1, so it is not fixed in the current release. It
had not been reported, and is now filed as
[rspatial/terra#2175](https://github.com/rspatial/terra/issues/2175).

It does not reproduce on synthetic data. On clean, hand-built polygons `union()` is exact. Only real
inventory geometry triggers it, so a passing test suite is no evidence that a call is safe.

It is a precision failure. Shifting the vertices by a single millimetre makes the answer come out
right, to within 0.14 m² of 12.3 million:

```{r union-precision}
data.frame(
  Tolerance = c("none", "1 mm", "1 cm", "10 cm", "1 m", "10 m"),
  `Counted twice (m2)` = c("56,640.5", "0.0", "0.0", "0.0", "0.0", "299.1"),
  `Error vs truth (m2)` = c("-12,030,541.2", "-0.1", "+0.3", "+6.9", "+1,222.6", "+8,570.4"),
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  styled(
    caption = paste(
      "Simplifying the inputs before the union, on the minimal case.",
      "A millimetre is far below the precision of the source data."
    ),
    booktabs = TRUE
  )
```

That last point offers a tempting workaround, and the pipeline deliberately does not use it. The
replacement, `overlay_left_join()`, is `intersect()` plus `erase()`: it partitions the input exactly
by construction rather than by luck, it is faster, and it does not depend on a tolerance that
happens to suit this data and silently stops working at 10 m.

The seven-polygon case, the figure above and the measurements are attached to
[rspatial/terra#2175](https://github.com/rspatial/terra/issues/2175), which was **fixed upstream on
2026-08-29**. The project now runs terra 1.9-48, installed from GitHub and pinned by commit in
`renv.lock`, and the fix is confirmed here: the minimal case goes from 56,640 m² of self-overlap to
0.000, and the study-area window from a 8,607 m² footprint error to 0.012 m².

## A second defect, in `terra::erase()`

Replacing `union()` was not the end of it. The rewritten step then ran for six hours and died with
`[[<-,SpatVector] cannot add these values`, which named neither a column nor a reason. The cause was
`terra::erase()` returning a `SpatVector` with **more attribute rows than geometries**: a polygon
whose difference comes out empty loses its geometry but keeps its row. Nothing reports it at the
time; whatever next reads the attributes fails instead.

It is a different bug from the first, and the fix for #2175 does not cover it: that fix moved
`union()` onto `erase_agg()`, which is the function R's `erase()` was already calling. Reported as
[rspatial/terra#2179](https://github.com/rspatial/terra/issues/2179), still open.

```{r erase-defect}
data.frame(
  Measure = c(
    "tiles where the overlay is consistent",
    "total time for the erase step",
    "agreement where terra succeeded"
  ),
  terra = c("37 of 42", "192.5 s", "--"),
  sf = c("42 of 42", "388.9 s", "0.000000 m2"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  styled(
    caption = paste(
      "Erasing with terra against erasing with sf, on the same 42 tiles.",
      "sf cannot desynchronise: its attributes are columns of the same data frame as the geometry."
    ),
    booktabs = TRUE
  )
```

The pipeline therefore uses `sf::st_difference()` for this one step, through `erase_polygons()`. An
earlier version tried terra first and fell back to sf only when the result was inconsistent; that
was dropped deliberately. It made the output depend on which tiles happened to trip a bug nobody can
characterise, and one code path is easier to trust than two. The measured cost of using sf
throughout is about twice the terra time on a step that tiles to roughly five minutes.

Two things about this defect are worth recording. It does not reproduce on synthetic geometry
either: hand-built degenerate polygons come back *invalid*, and terra handles those correctly. The
polygon that triggers it is a valid four-vertex ring with zero area, whose second and third vertices
differ by 1e-10 -- a line traced out and back. And the failure is silent by construction, which is
why the check now sits inside `overlay_left_join()`: it compares geometry and attribute counts after
every overlay and fails there, rather than letting a malformed object travel.

### Fixed upstream, after this work

`terra::erase()` was fixed in [`12df7fbd`](https://github.com/rspatial/terra/commit/12df7fbd4f85eb01faa02c580a31ce7e34275c6a).
That fix is **not** in the build this pipeline runs: `renv.lock` pins terra at `1a8843f`, which
carries the #2175 fix only, so the defect described above is present in the version that produced
these results -- which is why the workaround is still in place and still necessary.

The workaround has since been promoted to `spatialutils` as `erase_polygons()`, together with
`overlay_left_join()` and `keep_polygons()`.
It survives the fix on its own merits: it also tolerates an empty right-hand layer, and it drops the
non-polygonal residue an overlay can leave behind.
Neither of those is a terra defect.

The second of the two is worth recording because it bit during this work.
`sf::st_difference()` can return a bare `LINESTRING` sitting directly in the geometry column -- not
inside a `GEOMETRYCOLLECTION` -- when everything left of a polygon is a shared edge.
`terra::vect()` then drops that geometry while keeping its attribute row, producing exactly the
desynchronisation #2179 causes, from an entirely different direction.
Measured on one tile of the study area, one of 6,871 differences was such a line.
A guard testing only for `GEOMETRYCOLLECTION` misses it; `spatialutils::intersect_clean()` carried
the same too-narrow guard and has been fixed in the same release.

## Forest patches

```{r patches-table}
pub_gpkg <- file.path(PUBLISHED, "forest_patches_final.gpkg")
ok_patches <- have(pub_gpkg) &&
  !inherits(try(tar_read_raw("forest_patches_final"), silent = TRUE), "try-error") &&
  is_rebuilt("forest_patches_final")
```

```{r patches-compare, eval = ok_patches}
tabulate_patches <- function(v) {
  v$ha <- terra::expanse(v, unit = "ha", transform = FALSE)
  as.data.frame(v) |>
    group_by(Seral, Resistance, SourceWt) |>
    summarise(n = n(), ha = sum(ha), .groups = "drop")
}

b <- terra::vect(pub_gpkg)
a <- tidyterra::as_spatvector(tar_read_raw("forest_patches_final"))

cmp <- full_join(
  tabulate_patches(b) |> rename(n_pub = n, ha_pub = ha),
  tabulate_patches(a) |> rename(n_cor = n, ha_cor = ha),
  by = c("Seral", "Resistance", "SourceWt")
) |>
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric), \(x) ifelse(is.na(x), 0, x)),
    d = ha_cor - ha_pub,
    pct = ifelse(ha_pub > 0, 100 * d / ha_pub, NA_real_)
  ) |>
  arrange(Resistance)

cmp |>
  transmute(
    Seral,
    Resistance,
    SourceWt,
    `Published (ha)` = num(ha_pub),
    `Corrected (ha)` = num(ha_cor),
    `Change (ha)` = num(d),
    `Change (%)` = num(pct)
  ) |>
  styled(
    caption = paste(
      "Final resultant by seral stage. Resistance and source weight are assigned from the seral",
      "stage, so a stage that changes area moves that area between resistance classes."
    ),
    booktabs = TRUE
  )
```

```{r patches-missing, eval = !ok_patches, results = "asis"}
cat("_The corrected `forest_patches_final` was not available when this was rendered._\n")
```

## Patch statistics

Patch statistics now apply a 1 ha floor, matching the CEF Biodiversity Protocol threshold for
residual patches and the threshold arcpy `Eliminate` applies.
This is a reporting filter only: it never changes the layers the connectivity analysis is built
from, and the excluded count and area are reported alongside.

```{r patch-stats, results = "asis"}
pub_stats <- file.path(PUB_META, "Quesnel_TSA_seral_patch_stats.csv")
cor_stats <- file.path(proj, "Outputs", "Quesnel_TSA_seral_patch_stats.csv")
if (have(pub_stats, cor_stats)) {
  p <- read.csv(pub_stats)
  q <- read.csv(cor_stats)
  keep <- intersect(names(p), names(q))
  bind_rows(mutate(p[, keep], run = "published"), mutate(q[, keep], run = "corrected")) |>
    styled(caption = "Seral patch statistics, published vs corrected.", booktabs = TRUE) |>
    cat(sep = "\n")
} else {
  cat("_Patch statistics not available._")
}
```

# Runtime and resources

## Runtime

Times are CPU seconds as recorded by `targets`, summed over branches, so they exceed wall clock
wherever branches ran in parallel.
They are grouped by workflow stage rather than by target: the rewrite split, merged and removed
targets, so individual names do not line up between the two runs, and several stages now do in one
target what previously took three.

Two things have to be filtered out or the comparison is meaningless.
The store keeps metadata for targets that were *not rebuilt*, which would compare the published run
against itself; and it also keeps metadata for targets the rewrite *removed*, which counts
eliminated work as though it still ran.
Totals below are filtered against `tar_manifest()` -- the targets that exist in the pipeline today
-- with removed targets attributed to the stage they used to serve, so each row shows the net effect
of the change rather than a deletion and an addition side by side.

```{r runtime-stage, results = "asis"}
## Group targets into workflow stages. Order matters: first match wins.
stage_of <- function(x) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("^omniscape", x) ~ "Omniscape configuration",
    grepl("interpatch_distances|quantiles_|forest_patches_chunks|patches_matold", x) ~
      "Interpatch distances",
    grepl("^(resistance|sourcewt)_", x) ~ "Resistance and source-weight surfaces",
    grepl("^patches_|^patch_summary|^forest_patches_final", x) ~ "Patch construction",
    grepl("^forest_disturbance_seral", x) ~ "Seral classification",
    grepl("^VRI_BECNDT", x) ~ "VRI x NDT-BEC overlay",
    grepl("^(readme|reproducibility_receipt)$", x) ~ "Reporting",
    TRUE ~ "Input layers and study area"
  )
}

roll <- function(store) {
  m <- tar_meta(store = store, fields = c("name", "seconds", "parent"))
  br <- m |>
    filter(!is.na(parent)) |>
    group_by(name = parent) |>
    summarise(seconds = sum(seconds, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  tp <- m |> filter(is.na(parent), !is.na(seconds)) |> transmute(name, seconds)
  bind_rows(br, tp) |> group_by(name) |> summarise(seconds = max(seconds), .groups = "drop")
}

if (dir.exists(PUB_META)) {
  live <- tar_manifest()$name
  o <- roll(PUB_META) |> rename(pub = seconds)
  n <- roll(file.path(proj, "_targets")) |> filter(name %in% live) |> rename(cor = seconds)

  by_stage <- full_join(o, n, by = "name") |>
    mutate(stage = stage_of(name)) |>
    group_by(stage) |>
    summarise(
      pub = sum(pub, na.rm = TRUE) / 3600,
      cor = sum(cor, na.rm = TRUE) / 3600,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(chg = cor - pub) |>
    arrange(chg)

  tot <- summarise(by_stage, stage = "**Total**", pub = sum(pub), cor = sum(cor), chg = sum(chg))

  bind_rows(by_stage, tot) |>
    transmute(
      Stage = stage,
      Published = sprintf("%.1f h", pub),
      Corrected = sprintf("%.1f h", cor),
      Change = ifelse(abs(chg) < 0.05, "--", sprintf("%+.1f h", chg))
    ) |>
    styled(
      caption = "Pipeline cost by workflow stage, published against corrected (CPU hours).",
      booktabs = TRUE,
      row.names = FALSE,
      align = "lrrr"
    ) |>
    cat(sep = "\n")
}
```

**A full build costs about 90 CPU hours less than the published one**, despite the corrections
adding work, and nearly all of that comes from two stages.

*Interpatch distances* (-50 h) lost `all_interpatch_distances_chunks`, which held the distances in
memory as a list of chunks; they are now written straight to a parquet dataset.
The quantile step over that dataset was itself rewritten after it was OOM-killed six hours into a
run: asking DuckDB for five quantiles as five aggregates made it keep five sorted states at once and
peak at 336 GB, where one `quantile_cont()` call over a list of probabilities peaks at 28.7 GB and
returns bit-identical values.

*Patch construction* (-40 h) lost `patches_union_final_3` (33.5 h to change 12 polygons out of
162,905, and zero area), and `patches_union_final` itself went from 5 h 52 m to 18 m by tiling.

The one stage that got *slower* is the VRI x NDT-BEC overlay (+0.5 h).
That is the price of correctness: the arcpy LENGTH sliver rule is more expensive than the area rule
it replaced, and it now runs on more and smaller polygons because the seral layer no longer
collapses duplicates.

These are CPU hours, not wall clock.
Wall clock is not comparable between the two runs -- the published one was driven by hand, and the
corrected one shared a machine with an unrelated job.

## Tiling the final resultant

`patches_union_final` is the arcpy step-6 overlay: the seral layer joined to both interior-forest
layers.
It ran as a single process and took **5 h 51 m 58 s**.

The overlay is embarrassingly parallel over space, so it now branches over `study_area_tiles` -- the
same 8x8 grid the seral layer itself was built on -- and reads its base layer through GDAL rather
than out of the `targets` store, so a worker materialises only the polygons inside its own tile.

```{r tiling-cost, results = "asis"}
data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Runtime", "Branches", "Slowest branch", "Features", "Planar area"),
  Serial = c("5 h 51 m 58 s", "1", "--", "189,666", "2,473,003.272 ha"),
  Tiled = c("17 m 48 s", "49, all succeeding", "2 m 48 s", "192,683", "2,473,003.272 ha"),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  styled(
    caption = "Building the final resultant, serial against tiled.",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    row.names = FALSE,
    label = "tiling-cost"
  ) |>
  cat(sep = "\n")
```

**19.8x faster, with the area preserved exactly.**

Reusing the *same* grid is load-bearing, not a convenience.
The seral layer already carries vertices lying bit-exactly on these seam coordinates, so re-cutting
on the same grid intersects at existing vertices and GEOS invents no new ones; the halves of a split
polygon abut exactly and dissolve back together.
A finer grid would cut at fresh coordinates and forfeit that.

Cropping splits polygons at the seams, so the resultant carries 3,017 more features (+1.59%).
That is a change to a shipped artefact -- `forest_patches_final.gpkg` -- even though no hectare
moves.
It does not propagate: `calc_matold()` dissolves before the interpatch distances are measured.

The verification that matters is the distance distribution, since that is what sets the Omniscape
radii:

```{r tiling-quantiles, results = "asis"}
data.frame(
  Quantile = c("25%", "50%", "75%", "90%", "99%", "100%"),
  Serial = c(0.372, 12.500, 39.787, 91.901, 330.123, 2566.803),
  Tiled = c(0.464, 12.603, 39.899, 92.131, 330.685, 2566.803)
) |>
  transform(Difference = sprintf("%+.3f", Tiled - Serial)) |>
  styled(
    caption = paste(
      "Nearest-neighbour distance quantiles in metres, serial against tiled.",
      "The 100% row is the one the Omniscape radius is derived from."
    ),
    booktabs = TRUE,
    row.names = FALSE,
    label = "tiling-quantiles"
  ) |>
  cat(sep = "\n")
```

Every quantile agrees to under a metre, and q100 -- the one `omniscape_config_nndist` actually
consumes -- is identical.
The radius is unchanged either way.

Dissolving does move slightly: `patches_matold` comes out 68,255 patches tiled against 68,401
serial.
This is the dissolve, not the tiling.
Before the dissolve the two layers agree to **0.000000 ha**; after it, the *serial* dissolve has
gained 0.798 ha, which a dissolve cannot do.
`terra::aggregate()` is simply not exact on a layer of this size -- the same layers self-overlap by
about 10 ha out of 2.47 Mha in both builds.

## Tiling the interior-forest overlay

The final resultant was not the only overlay of this shape.
`patches_interior_forest_old` and `patches_interior_forest_mature_old` erase a buffer mask from the
old and mature+old patch layers, and between them they cost **8.1 CPU hours** in the corrected run --
3 h 07 m and 5 h 00 m respectively.
They were the largest remaining single-target costs once the resultant was tiled.

The cause is structural rather than incidental.
`patches_create_erase_mask()` rbinds the four buffer layers and dissolves them with
`terra::aggregate()`, which leaves the mask as a **single multipolygon covering 2,401,307.9 ha** --
the whole study area.
The cost of a difference is superlinear in the complexity of the layer being subtracted, so each of
the 42,764 patches was differenced against study-area-wide geometry no matter how small the patch
itself was.

Cropping both sides to a tile first shrinks the mask each difference sees to tile size.
It reuses the same 49-tile grid as the resultant, for the same reason given above.

```{r interior-tiling-cost, results = "asis"}
data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Runtime", "Tiles", "Slowest tile", "Features", "Planar area"),
  Untiled = c("3 h 07 m 34 s", "1", "--", "10,263", "167,496.729062 ha"),
  Tiled = c("6 m 08 s", "49, all succeeding", "1 m 27 s", "10,263", "167,496.729059 ha"),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  styled(
    caption = paste(
      "Building the old interior-forest layer, untiled against tiled.",
      "Sequential in both cases, so the tiled column is compute, not parallelism."
    ),
    booktabs = TRUE,
    row.names = FALSE,
    label = "interior-tiling-cost"
  ) |>
  cat(sep = "\n")
```

**30.5x faster, with the same 10,263 features and the area agreeing to 1.5e-11 relative** -- three
parts in a hundred billion, which is floating-point noise rather than a difference.
Unlike the resultant, the feature count does not change: the layer is dissolved after the tiles are
combined rather than per tile, so halves split at a seam are rejoined before anything downstream
sees them.

Tiling is only valid because this overlay is *local*: which part of a patch survives depends solely
on mask geometry near that patch.
The same treatment would be wrong for the dissolve or the interpatch distances, where a feature's
result depends on the whole layer.

The per-tile spread is the useful diagnostic: 0.2 s at the fastest, 2.8 s median, 87.5 s at the
slowest.
A factor of 31 between median and worst says cost is driven by local mask complexity rather than by
patch count, which is what makes the untiled form scale so badly -- every patch pays the worst case.

### Why this matters beyond Quesnel

Quesnel is the smallest of the Cariboo districts this workflow is intended to cover.
Cariboo-Chilcotin is roughly **2.4 times** its area, and the costs above do not scale with area:
the mask for a larger district is both larger and more intricate, and the superlinearity is in mask
complexity, not in patch count.
At the untiled cost profile, the interior-forest pair alone would plausibly dominate an entire
district build, and it is not the only overlay of this shape in the workflow.

This retooling is therefore a **prerequisite** for extending the analysis beyond Quesnel rather
than an optimisation of it.
The arithmetic is unforgiving in the other direction too: a step that takes a day is not merely slow,
it is a step that cannot be retried casually when something downstream needs changing, and this
report exists because several things did need changing.

One caveat on reading the runtime table above against this section: the stored Quesnel results were
built with the untiled code, so the table reports what that build actually cost.
The figures here are measured on the same inputs and verified to reproduce the stored output exactly,
but they are not what produced the numbers elsewhere in this report.

## Memory

Measured by sampling the resident set size of every project R process every 30 seconds across the
rerun, rather than estimated.

```{r memory}
data.frame(
  Measure = c(
    "Peak aggregate RSS",
    "Largest single process",
    "Typical during tiled overlays",
    "terra ceiling per worker (`BC_CONN_MEMFRAC=0.01`)"
  ),
  Value = c("110.0 GB", "41.1 GB", "~1.5 GB per branch", "~10 GB"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  styled(
    caption = paste(
      "Memory use of the data-preparation pipeline with 8 workers.",
      "Omniscape is excluded: it is opt-in and needs hundreds of GB."
    ),
    booktabs = TRUE
  )
```

# Implications for Omniscape

Omniscape consumes exactly two rasters: the composite resistance surface and the composite source
weights.
Both are assigned from `Seral`, so any area that changes seral stage moves between resistance
classes, and the connectivity result changes with it.

```{r omniscape-rasters}
pr <- file.path(PUBLISHED, "rasters", "resistance_composite_30.tif")
cr <- file.path(proj, "Data", "processed", "rasters", "resistance_composite_30.tif")
## The corrected composite is written by the `resistance_composite` target; until that has been
## rebuilt the file on disk is still the published one, and comparing it with its own backup would
## report no change at all.
ok_rast <- have(pr, cr) && is_rebuilt("resistance_composite")
```

```{r omniscape-diff, eval = ok_rast, results = "asis"}
rb <- terra::rast(pr)
rn <- terra::rast(cr)
if (terra::compareGeom(rb, rn, stopOnError = FALSE)) {
  d <- rn - rb
  chg <- terra::global(d != 0, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]
  tot <- terra::global(!is.na(d), "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]]
  cellha <- prod(terra::res(rb)) / 1e4
  data.frame(
    Measure = c(
      "cells compared",
      "cells changed",
      "share of study area changed",
      "area changed (ha)",
      "mean resistance, published",
      "mean resistance, corrected"
    ),
    Value = c(
      num(tot, 0),
      num(chg, 0),
      paste0(num(100 * chg / tot, 2), " %"),
      num(chg * cellha, 0),
      num(terra::global(rb, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]], 2),
      num(terra::global(rn, "mean", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]], 2)
    ),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) |>
    styled(caption = "Change in the composite resistance surface at 30 m.", booktabs = TRUE) |>
    cat(sep = "\n")
}
```

```{r omniscape-pending, eval = !ok_rast, results = "asis"}
cat("_The corrected resistance surface had not been rebuilt when this was rendered._\n")
```

## Run naming

Omniscape run directories are stamped with `OMNISCAPE_VINTAGE`, set in `_targets.R`.
It was previously a hardcoded `"2026-01-23"`, which is the vintage of the published runs.
Because `run_omniscape()` deletes an existing output directory before running, a corrected run whose
radius matched a published one would have destroyed it -- and there are 17 GB of published results,
four of them under that prefix, including the run the report was written from.
Corrected runs are stamped `2026-08-26`.

## Radii

The Omniscape `radius`, `block_size` and `buffer` are all in **pixels**, not map units.
Radii are derived from quantiles of the interpatch distance distribution, so the corrected patches
imply new radii and hence new run names.

**Both radii move**, and by more than a pixel.

The published values are recoverable independently of any stored quantile, because
`write_omniscape_config()` stamps the radius into the run directory name: the `2026-01-23` vintage
wrote `p30_r1507_bs151` (regional) and `p30_r58_bs7` / `p90_r20_bs3` (local).

```{r radii, results = "asis"}
ok_q <- is_rebuilt("quantiles_nn_dists") && is_rebuilt("quantiles_all_dists")
qn <- try(tar_read_raw("quantiles_nn_dists"), silent = TRUE)
qa <- try(tar_read_raw("quantiles_all_dists"), silent = TRUE)

if (ok_q && !inherits(qn, "try-error") && !inherits(qa, "try-error")) {
  ## `use_radius()` takes the quantile in METRES and returns pixels, so the pin is resolution-
  ## independent: the same distance gives a different pixel count at 30 m and at 90 m.
  px <- function(m, res) ceiling(m / res)

  nn100 <- as.numeric(qn[["100%"]])
  all25 <- as.numeric(qa[["25%"]])

  ## published metres, back-derived from the run names above (radius px * pixel size)
  pub <- data.frame(
    Quantity = c("Regional (all-pairs q25)", "Local (nearest-neighbour q100)"),
    `Published m` = c(45202, 1726),
    `Corrected m` = c(all25, nn100),
    `px at 30 m` = c(sprintf("1507 -> %d", px(all25, 30)), sprintf("58 -> %d", px(nn100, 30))),
    `px at 90 m` = c(sprintf("503 -> %d", px(all25, 90)), sprintf("20 -> %d", px(nn100, 90))),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  pub$`Published m` <- num(pub$`Published m`, 0)
  pub$`Corrected m` <- num(pub$`Corrected m`, 0)

  cat(
    styled(
      pub,
      caption = "Radii before and after the corrections.",
      booktabs = TRUE,
      row.names = FALSE,
      label = "radii-change"
    ),
    sep = "\n"
  )
  cat("\n\n")

  show_q <- function(x, cap, lbl) {
    d <- as.data.frame(x)
    if (nrow(d) > 20) {
      d <- d[seq(1, nrow(d), length.out = 20), , drop = FALSE]
    }
    ## an explicit label per table: three tables come out of this one chunk, and knitr labels
    ## them all with the chunk name otherwise, so every cross-reference resolves to the last one
    cat(styled(d, caption = cap, booktabs = TRUE, row.names = FALSE, label = lbl), sep = "\n")
    cat("\n\n")
  }
  show_q(qn, "Nearest-neighbour interpatch distance quantiles (corrected).", "quantiles-nn")
  show_q(qa, "All-pairs interpatch distance quantiles (corrected).", "quantiles-all")
} else {
  cat(
    "_Distance quantiles had not been rebuilt when this was rendered;",
    "the radii for the corrected runs are therefore not yet known._\n"
  )
}
```

The regional radius falls by 5.2% and the local one rises by 49%.
Neither is within the roughly one-pixel slack that would leave the pixel count unchanged, so every
corrected run needs its own configuration -- which is what the four `2026-08-26` directories are.

The direction differs because the two quantiles measure different things.
The all-pairs q25 fell because the corrected patch set covers less area overall; the
nearest-neighbour q100 is a **maximum**, and maxima are sensitive to the patch-construction defect
in a way that interior quantiles are not.

This is entirely a consequence of the corrections, not of tiling: the serial and tiled builds give
q100 identical to the millimetre (see "Tiling the final resultant").

## What the corrections did to the published maps

The published inputs were copied aside before the rerun overwrote them, and the published runs
survived because the corrections changed the run names, so the effect of the fix on the Omniscape
result can be measured rather than argued about.
The figures below are for the regional run at 30 m, which is the run the published reporting was
written from.

```{r omniscape-summary-setup}
RAST_PUB <- file.path(PUBLISHED, "rasters")
RAST_CUR <- file.path(proj, "Data", "processed", "rasters")
RUN_PUB <- file.path(proj, "Outputs", "2026-01-23_p30_r1507_bs151")
RUN_COR <- file.path(proj, "Outputs", "2026-08-26_p30_r1429_bs143")

ok_summary <- dir.exists(RAST_PUB) &&
  is_rebuilt("resistance_composite") &&
  all(file.exists(file.path(c(RUN_PUB, RUN_COR), "normalized_cum_currmap.tif")))

## Prose below quotes these inline; NA defaults keep a skipped chunk from failing the render.
osum <- stats::setNames(
  rep(NA_real_, 8),
  c(
    "ha_chg",
    "pct_chg",
    "ha_net_extent",
    "ha_best",
    "ha_matrix",
    "r_norm",
    "ha_cross",
    "parks"
  )
)

## Several of these can go either way; let the number decide its own sign rather than baking one in.
signed <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(ifelse(!is.na(x) & x >= 0, "+", ""), num(x, d))
```

```{r omniscape-summary, eval = ok_summary}
## One read per raster into a plain vector, rather than repeated `terra::global()` passes that
## re-read the file for every statistic. Only the regional 30 m pair is compared here -- it is
## the run the published reporting was written from.
vals <- function(f) terra::values(terra::rast(f), mat = FALSE)
cellha <- 30 * 30 / 1e4

## gc() returns its summary matrix, and this chunk's results are printed -- without invisible()
## three memory tables land in the middle of the section.

## composite resistance: what Omniscape actually reads
ca <- vals(file.path(RAST_PUB, "resistance_composite_30.tif"))
cb <- vals(file.path(RAST_CUR, "resistance_composite_30.tif"))
osum[["ha_chg"]] <- sum(ca != cb) * cellha
osum[["pct_chg"]] <- 100 * mean(ca != cb)
osum[["ha_best"]] <- (sum(cb == 1) - sum(ca == 1)) * cellha
osum[["ha_matrix"]] <- (sum(cb == 1000) - sum(ca == 1000)) * cellha
rm(ca, cb)
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

## forest layer: NA off-patch, so its NA count is the patch extent
fa <- vals(file.path(RAST_PUB, "resistance_forest_30.tif"))
fb <- vals(file.path(RAST_CUR, "resistance_forest_30.tif"))
osum[["ha_net_extent"]] <- (sum(!is.na(fb)) - sum(!is.na(fa))) * cellha
rm(fa, fb)
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

## normalized current: the product, and the layer the project's summaries are built on
na_ <- vals(file.path(RUN_PUB, "normalized_cum_currmap.tif"))
nb_ <- vals(file.path(RUN_COR, "normalized_cum_currmap.tif"))
ok <- !is.na(na_) & !is.na(nb_)
na_ <- na_[ok]
nb_ <- nb_[ok]
osum[["r_norm"]] <- stats::cor(na_, nb_)
## 1.0 is the only non-arbitrary breakpoint: above it current exceeds flow potential
## (channelized), below it falls short (impeded), so a cell that crosses changes interpretation.
osum[["ha_cross"]] <- sum((na_ > 1) != (nb_ > 1)) * cellha
rm(na_, nb_, ok)
invisible(gc(verbose = FALSE))

## the project's own downstream metric, for the protected-areas network
zp <- function(d) {
  z <- utils::read.csv(file.path(d, "zonal_by_polys.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  z$mean_norm_cum_curr[z$zone == "parks"]
}
if (all(file.exists(file.path(c(RUN_PUB, RUN_COR), "zonal_by_polys.csv")))) {
  osum[["parks"]] <- 100 * (zp(RUN_COR) / zp(RUN_PUB) - 1)
}
```

```{r omniscape-summary-table, eval = ok_summary, results = "asis"}
data.frame(
  Measure = c(
    "Composite resistance surface changed",
    "Share of the study area",
    "Net change in forest patch extent",
    "Area moving to the best resistance class",
    "Area moving to the matrix class",
    "Correlation, published vs corrected normalized current",
    "Area crossing normalized current = 1",
    "Change in mean normalized current within parks"
  ),
  Value = c(
    paste(num(osum[["ha_chg"]], 0), "ha"),
    paste0(num(osum[["pct_chg"]], 1), " %"),
    paste(signed(osum[["ha_net_extent"]], 0), "ha"),
    paste(signed(osum[["ha_best"]], 0), "ha"),
    paste(signed(osum[["ha_matrix"]], 0), "ha"),
    num(osum[["r_norm"]], 2),
    paste(num(osum[["ha_cross"]], 0), "ha"),
    paste0(signed(osum[["parks"]], 1), " %")
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  styled(
    caption = paste(
      "Effect of the corrections on the Omniscape inputs and outputs, regional run at 30 m.",
      "Patch extent is measured from the forest resistance layer, which is NA off-patch."
    ),
    booktabs = TRUE,
    label = "omniscape-summary"
  ) |>
  cat(sep = "\n")
```

```{r omniscape-summary-pending, eval = !ok_summary, results = "asis"}
cat("_The published and corrected artefacts were not both available when this was rendered._\n")
```

Three things in that table carry into the district extension.

**The correction polarises the landscape rather than shifting it.**
The best resistance class more than doubles and the matrix grows, both at the expense of the
middle classes.
Because the gains at each end largely cancel, the mean of the composite moves by under 2% while
`r num(osum[["pct_chg"]], 1)`% of the study area changes class.

**The district-wide output totals barely move while the map underneath them does.**
The mean of the normalized current map changes by no more than a few percent, but the cell-by-cell
correlation between the published and corrected maps is `r num(osum[["r_norm"]], 2)`, and
`r num(osum[["ha_cross"]], 0)` ha cross the value of 1 that separates a channelized cell from an
impeded one.
The corrected run finds about as much channelized land as the published one did, in different
places.

**The zone-level conclusions do not survive.**
Mean normalized current within the protected-areas network moves by
`r signed(osum[["parks"]], 1)`%, and across the Landscape Unit by BEC zone summaries the median zone
barely moves while a tenth of them move by more than half.
Those summaries, not the rasters, are what the reporting was written from.

That last point is why the published maps are superseded rather than refined.
It is also the argument for building the extension to Cariboo-Chilcotin on the corrected pipeline
rather than reconciling it against the published Quesnel run afterwards: a reconciliation at this
scale is not a correction factor, it is a rerun.

# Reproducing this report

This report is deliberately **not** a pipeline target: it compares two runs, one of which no longer
exists as a live `targets` store.
It reads:

- `Data/processed/published-2026-01-27/` -- the published patches layer, composite rasters and map,
  copied aside before the rerun overwrote them;
- the `targets` metadata snapshot of the published run;
- the live `_targets` store for the corrected values.

Render with:

The rendered PDF is written to `Outputs/`, not next to the source, so it lands on the shared volume
alongside the other results rather than inside the clone:

```{r render-cmd, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
rmarkdown::render(
  "reports/corrections-2026-08.Rmd",
  output_file = "corrections-2026-08.pdf",
  output_dir = "Outputs"
)
```

```{r session}
data.frame(
  Item = c("R", "targets", "terra", "sf", "git branch", "git commit"),
  Value = c(
    as.character(getRversion()),
    as.character(packageVersion("targets")),
    as.character(packageVersion("terra")),
    as.character(packageVersion("sf")),
    system("git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD", intern = TRUE),
    system("git rev-parse --short HEAD", intern = TRUE)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  styled(caption = "Environment.", booktabs = TRUE)
```
